statusDetail: Complete atomic audit of 58 checks across five representative news paths.

page.framework: Server-rendered MPA with extensive vendor JavaScript
page.notes: Public Spanish news publication. The homepage, section, article, latest-news feed and a representative HTTP error state were covered. Search, checkout, cancellation, authenticated account settings, video playback and game completion were not covered because they are separate hosts, gated journeys or distinct product templates.

paths.description: Homepage and lead-story discovery, representing the primary news landing template.
España section, representing section and topic-listing templates.
Current España news article, representing the article and reading journey.
Latest-news listing, representing the chronological feed journey.
Missing sitemap URL returning the site 404 template, used as a representative HTTP failure state.

findings.summary: The site stays light when the user requests dark mode.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshots are pixel-identical in palette to the light screenshots; the probe reports color-scheme normal and no prefers-color-scheme CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define a prefers-color-scheme dark palette with light-dark() or equivalent tokens.

findings.summary: Route and menu state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no view-transition rules, while navigation is a core interaction across the MPA.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document transitions for menu state and progressive cross-document transitions for article navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The horizontal game carousel is script-driven without platform scroll snapping.
findings.evidence: The mobile probe found an initialized Swiper with a transformed wrapper, but no scroll-snap CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap and overscroll behavior, retaining controls as an enhancement.

findings.summary: The long news page has no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress cue.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query or scroll progress implementation across a 15,712px homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight article/page progress cue and make sticky chrome respond to scroll state.

findings.summary: A fixed subscription promotion obscures primary content on the homepage.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a fixed subscription banner covering the lower 175px, about 22% of the mobile viewport, immediately on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not cover content on load. Move the offer inline or use a user-invoked, semantic, light-dismissible popover.

findings.summary: The subscription interruption is an ad-hoc fixed aside rather than a semantic overlay.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe identifies ASIDE#banda_suscripcion as a fixed 360x175 overlay; no dialog or popover primitive is used.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog or popover semantics with an accessible name, explicit close control, focus behavior, and light dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Mobile layouts create a document twice the viewport width.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence on both homepage and article reports scrollWidth 720px at innerWidth 360px, with 360px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Contain carousels and off-canvas navigation without widening the root, then use intrinsic sizing and fluid/container-relative dimensions.

findings.summary: Repeated cards and navigation rely on viewport rules, not component containment.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no @container or container-type despite card components being reused across homepage, section, and sidebars.
findings.suggestedFix: Add inline-size containment to reusable card regions and size them with container queries.

findings.summary: Several mobile controls are too small or tightly spaced.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size failed; the focus probe also measured many topical links at only 11px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas and spacing to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls, while keeping visible focus.

findings.summary: The primary landing page is very slow and main-thread heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 28.6s, FCP 10.7s, TBT 1,120ms and a 0.32 performance score; the CDP trace corroborated a 563ms longest task and 549ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the lead content, defer nonessential scripts, split long tasks, and set explicit performance budgets.

findings.summary: Late homepage UI causes severe observed layout movement.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded CLS 2.001 with two late shifts of 1.0 around 6.5s, coinciding with late fixed/personalization UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late modules and prevent overlays or experimentation code from moving the document.

findings.summary: The page ships an oversized, third-party-dominated dependency graph.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 264 requests and 4.71MB transferred, including 82 scripts totaling 3.41MB; Lighthouse estimated 4.92s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential tags, defer or conditionally load advertising/media SDKs, consolidate fonts, and improve cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Large amounts of JavaScript are unused during the initial news-reading task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,480KiB of unused JavaScript and 35KiB unused CSS; third-party scripts dominate the largest transfer list.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route and interaction-based loading, deduplicate tag bundles, and remove code not needed for initial reading.

findings.summary: Embedded frames and many images lack accessible text alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed frame-title; the article probe found multiple untitled advertising/paywall iframes, and the images primitive counted 33 images without alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Title every meaningful iframe, hide technical frames from assistive technology where safe, and provide meaningful or empty alt text based on image purpose.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during a normal load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console, and HAR hygiene recorded SSL, ORB, aborted analytics, and localhost connection failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove broken integrations, guard optional vendors, and monitor uncaught errors in production.

findings.summary: Some images lack intrinsic dimensions and the document uses a legacy encoding.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found three images without width/height; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images. The document reports ISO-8859-15 rather than UTF-8.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve UTF-8 and add width/height or aspect-ratio for every content image.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and platform lifecycle blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecation warnings, two BFCache failure reasons, and DevTools inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use, address unload or cache-control BFCache blockers, and resolve surfaced inspector issues.

findings.summary: Some visible actions are exposed as hash links rather than crawlable destinations.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors; the article probe counted 45 href="#" anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and real destination URLs for navigation.

findings.summary: No sitemap is advertised at the conventional endpoint or in robots.txt.
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returned 404 and the fetched robots.txt contained no Sitemap declaration, while pages themselves had valid canonicals and index directives.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish sitemap indexes for current article and section URLs and declare them in robots.txt.

findings.summary: Core security headers are absent and cookies are broadly insecure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection, or Permissions-Policy and found Referrer-Policy unsafe-url. All 44 observed cookies were flagged insecure by the cookie audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a minimal Permissions-Policy; mark HTTPS cookies Secure with suitable SameSite and HttpOnly.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising dominate the initial page load.
findings.evidence: The tracker audit found 64 third-party origins and 14 known tracker hosts. HAR classified 255 of 264 requests and 4.61MB of 4.71MB as third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, gate nonessential tracking on valid consent, batch analytics, and load advertising only near relevant slots.

findings.summary: The visible sign-in surface has no detectable passkey/WebAuthn support.
findings.evidence: No passkey, WebAuthn, or navigator.credentials marker appeared in the server HTML, although sign-in is a prominent account action; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys as a first-class sign-in option and keep all permission requests tied to explicit user actions.

findings.summary: The subscription teaser does not disclose the price after the introductory month in context.
findings.evidence: The fixed offer says 0.50 euros per month and more than 90% discount, but the visible viewport does not state the renewal price or commitment.
findings.suggestedFix: Show the renewal price, billing cadence, cancellation terms, and total commitment beside the subscribe action.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently responsive or modern.
findings.evidence: The images audit found 36 images without srcset, 44 legacy-format image URLs, no modern-format img sources, and eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive picture/srcset delivery, AVIF/WebP where beneficial, dimensions, and lazy loading below the fold.

findings.summary: Third-party resource use is disproportionate to initial article discovery.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 4.61MB and 255 requests, including many advertising, experimentation, social and analytics SDKs before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove duplicate tags, and defer vendors until consent or user intent makes them necessary.

findings.summary: Repeated menu toggling leaves measurable growth after the interaction ends.
findings.evidence: Within one session, ten open/close cycles increased DOM elements from 2,824 to 2,854 and used JS heap from 70.7MB to 82.5MB. Separate heap snapshots grew from 69.1MB to 72.3MB self size.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained objects after menu teardown, remove generated nodes/listeners, and ensure vendor callbacks are not re-registered per toggle.

findings.summary: The baseline memory footprint is heavy for a mobile news landing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap snapshot contained 1,168,886 heap nodes and 69.1MB self size after load, alongside 3.41MB of transferred scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial JavaScript and vendor allocation, virtualize or defer deep-feed modules, and establish a mobile heap budget.

taskList.title: Cut and defer third-party JavaScript, tracking and ad work
Fix mobile root overflow and touch target sizing
Add security headers and secure cookie attributes
Remove or relocate the load-time subscription overlay
Improve image semantics and responsive delivery
Repair crawlability and publish sitemap indexes
Adopt progressive modern navigation and gesture primitives
Resolve console, deprecation and lifecycle defects
Profile and clean up retained menu state
